intro: Water is recovery work. Hydration supports energy, digestion, training, and clearer thinking — and it is one of the easiest daily wins to log.
buddyTip: Front-load a glass in the morning and pair water with each meal so you are not playing catch-up at 9pm.
mission: Log water on Home with your meals today — aim for steady sips, not a late chug.
why: Mild dehydration often feels like fatigue, headaches, or snacky hunger. People reach for food when a glass of water and a pause would have helped. Hydration will not replace sleep or protein — but it removes a common false signal.

Fibre needs fluid. Training needs fluid. Hot days and air travel increase needs. A fixed “eight glasses” myth is less useful than responsive drinking plus pale-straw urine as a rough guide (medications and vitamins can change colour).
Logging water builds the same honesty muscle as logging food. It is a low-stakes way to keep the daily ritual alive.

points: Drink across the day; huge late boluses mostly mean night bathroom trips
Thirst, climate, sweat, and diet (salty/high-fibre) change needs
Tea and coffee contribute fluid for most people; alcohol dehydrates relatively
Electrolytes matter more in heavy sweat or long endurance — not every office day
Water logging is a habit cue, not a competition

misconceptions.myth: If I’m hungry, I’m always actually thirsty.
misconceptions.truth: Sometimes true, not always. Check water, then check protein/fibre timing — both matter.
Unsweetened tea/coffee generally count toward fluid. Sugary drinks add energy you should log as intake.

steps: Glass on waking; water visible at your desk or bag
Use Home’s water quick action so hydration stays in the same daily desk
On training days, drink before you feel wiped — not only after
If evenings are dry-mouthed, move intake earlier rather than chugging in bed
how.buddyHelps: Home water actions keep hydration next to meal logging. Recovery-minded coaching treats water as part of the Health Operating System, not an afterthought.

sections.title: Scale weight and water
paras: Higher carb or salt days hold more water. That is not instant fat. Hydration status also shifts morning weight.
Use weekly trends for fat-loss decisions; use daily water for how you feel.

sections.title: Travel and heat
paras: Planes and heat silently increase needs. Carry a bottle and order water with meals out — boring, effective.

mistakes.quote: I drank two litres at once to “catch up.”
mistakes.why: Boluses are uncomfortable and poorly timed. Steady intake wins.

mistakes.quote: I replaced meals with water to lose faster.
mistakes.why: That is restriction, not hydration strategy. It harms training and invites rebound.

mistakes.quote: I ignore water because it’s not macros.
mistakes.why: Recovery nutrients include fluid. Feeling better improves adherence to everything else.

encouragement: Sip through the day and log it without drama. Hydration is one of the kindest habits you can automate.
